text: Element [Lat. elementum ]: Ger. Element ; Fr. élément ; Ital. elemento . That which cannot be reduced to simpler terms under the conditions of the investigation. In science the term refers to the different kinds of atoms, the sorts of material, of which the world is composed. See MATTER. During the ancient and mediaeval periods earth, air, fire, water constituted the elements. In logic the simplest idea which enters into a conception or system of conceptions is called an element of that conception or system. ( H.R.S. )
